CARB offers various modern interview options, including remote phone and video interviews. Join CARB and help us improve the lives of all Californians.

Department Website: http://www.arb.ca.gov

Job Description And Duties

This position can be located in Sacramento or Riverside County.

The In-Use Control Measures (IUCM) Section in the Transportation and Clean Technology Branch within the Mobile Source Control Division is looking for a dynamic individual with a strong work ethic, ability to analyze scientific data, and collaborative skills necessary to navigate complex rulemakings. The successful candidate will join a dynamic team responsible for developing and implementing regulatory strategies and emission control measures to support the reduction of harmful criteria and greenhouse gas emissions from medium- and heavy-duty trucks and buses. This section, comprised of Air Resources Engineers, Air Pollution Specialists, and Air Resources Technicians, is also responsible for supporting implementation and outreach of CARB's regulations affecting trucks and buses. As part of these efforts, the section works with internal CARB partners, federal, state, local agencies, engine manufacturers, vehicle operators, industry and environmental groups, state legislature, and other stakeholders.

This Air Pollution Specialist position requires an understanding of California's regulatory process, well-developed technical writing skills, and the ability to analyze large data set skills along with the ability to communicate those results and findings effectively. The incumbent will develop a variety of reports, briefing papers, speeches and presentations, and will work with management to research and recommend creative solutions to reduce the impacts of air pollution and climate change for the public and communities in California. The Air Pollution Specialist may also assist with researching information and preparing documents in support Division and Branch priorities for budgets, contracts, and other projects.

Job Description And Duties

Caltrans Environmental Scientists perform a broad range of work concerning environmental issues related to protecting California's resources as related to transportation projects. Incumbents do field analyses; prepare environmental documents and technical studies, environmental permitting packages and regulatory permits; ensure compliance with various environmental laws and regulations; and conduct environmental protection, planning, and mitigation activities. Incumbents apply scientific methods and principles to analyze and evaluate available data on the effects of transportation projects on all aspects of the environment; prepare and review CEQA/NEPA and other technical documents to determine the effects; and implement mitigation strategies to lessen the impact of those projects.

Under the general supervision of the Environmental Branch Chief, the incumbent is an interdisciplinary team member who must establish and maintain a professional working relationship with internal project delivery partners, various regulatory agencies, local partners and interested parties involved with Caltrans' projects. The incumbent must be solution oriented and will need to investigate innovative solutions to meet deliverables. This work requires strong oral and written skills with the specific ability to prepare technical reports as well as written and verbal correspondence. This position may require site visits, sometimes to remote areas, which may require driving a personal or state vehicle on public roadways or on uneven terrain.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
We're partnering with a well-established manufacturing organization to hire an experienced Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist for an extended temporary assignment of up to 6 months. This role is ideal for a hands-on safety professional who enjoys working closely with employees on the production floor while supporting environmental compliance and workplace safety initiatives.

What You'll Do

Support site environmental, health, and safety programs and initiatives
Assist with compliance activities related to federal, state, and local environmental and safety regulations
Prepare and maintain environmental reports, records, and permit documentation
Conduct safety inspections, audits, and workplace assessments
Support incident investigations and track corrective actions
Monitor EHS metrics and assist with continuous improvement efforts
Help administer environmental and safety programs, including employee training
Partner with supervisors and employees to promote a positive safety culture
Support new hire safety orientation and ongoing employee education
Maintain EHS documentation and compliance records

What We're Looking For

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field preferred
3+ years of EHS experience in a manufacturing, industrial, or production environment
Knowledge of environmental compliance programs, including:
Environmental permitting and reporting
Hazardous waste management
Wastewater compliance and reporting
Stormwater programs
Air quality compliance
Familiarity with OSHA, EPA, DEQ, DOT, and related regulatory requirements
Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills
Ability to build relationships and influence safe work practices across all levels of the organization

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in manufacturing or other regulated industrial environments
Exposure to Process Safety Management (PSM) programs
Knowledge of Lockout/Tagout, Confined Space, and Hot Work Permit programs
Experience conducting employee safety training
Strong Microsoft Office skills, including Excel

Schedule & Compensation

Pay:
$40-$41/hour
Duration:
Up to 6 months (extended temporary assignment)
Schedule:
Monday-Friday
Potential for a long-term opportunity for the right candidate
